To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a novel threshold-based admission-control algorithm for two classes of requests is presented and the optimal threshold values can be found by using the analytical models.

(i) the proposed algorithm can achieve higher performance than the existing threshold-based algorithm; (ii) the proposed analytical models are capable of finding the sub-optimal solution to the problem of finding the best threshold values; and (iii) the proposed algorithm is able to adapt to the changes of system workload by adjusting the threshold values.
the proposed algorithm can be used to improve the overall system performance by maximizing net earning value.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the performance evaluation of a novel threshold-based admission algorithm with negotiation for a multimedia server with two classes of requests.
the performance evaluation of an admission-control algorithm for a multimedia system.

the design and performance analysis of an admission control scheme that is capable of accepting high-priority clients with high probability, and at the same time, maintaining the QoS of low-priority clients.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed admission control algorithm with threshold-based negotiation mechanism can be dynamically adjusted, to optimize the system performance based upon the characteristics of the workload.
the proposed admission control algorithm with threshold-based negotiation is able to achieve higher system throughput and net earnings than existing algorithms.
the proposed algorithm can be used to achieve higher system throughput and higher net reward, while satisfying the QoS requirements.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a novel admission control algorithm with dynamic threshold and negotiation is proposed.

, in a system with two classes of requests, the admission control algorithm with threshold-based dynamic partition and negotiation mechanism can achieve higher net earning value than the conventional threshold-based admission control algorithms.
a dynamic threshold with negotiation algorithm for two priority classes is proposed.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the proposed admission control algorithm is capable of optimizing system performance based on different system objectives.
the proposed algorithm can dynamically adjust the system performance to adapt to the changes in the characteristics of the workload.

the system performance can be improved significantly when the server capacity is allocated to different classes of requests according to their priorities and the QoS requirements are negotiated to accept more high-priority clients.
